text: Production token rotation procedure. Rotating a production API token requires approval from the platform team. Run the rotation job, verify the new token in staging, then revoke the previous one after the grace period expires.

API token creation procedure. To create a new API token, open the console, choose a scope, and set an expiry. Newly created tokens are active immediately. Creation requires an account with the developer role.
API authentication overview. Every request to the API must carry a bearer token in the Authorization header. Requests without a valid token receive a 401 response.
Storing secrets. Secrets are held in the managed vault and injected at deploy time as environment variables. Never commit a secret to the repository.
Account credential policy. User passwords must be at least sixteen characters and are checked against a breach corpus. Credentials expire after one year.

Worker crash recovery. When a worker process dies, the supervisor detects the missing heartbeat and reschedules in-flight tasks onto a healthy worker. Partial work is discarded and the task restarts from its last checkpoint.
Worker configuration. Each worker reads its concurrency limit and queue bindings from the deployment manifest. Changing worker configuration requires a rolling restart.
Retry policy. Failed tasks are retried with exponential backoff up to five attempts. After the final attempt the task moves to the dead letter queue.
Temporal workflow basics. Workflows are deterministic functions whose state is reconstructed by replaying history. Activities perform the side effects.
Rolling back a deployment. Use the rollback command with the previous release identifier. Rollback reverts the container image but does not revert database migrations.
Database migrations. Migrations run before the new release receives traffic. A migration must be backward compatible with the previously deployed application version.
Invoices and billing cycles. Invoices are generated on the first day of each month and cover the preceding period. Usage is metered hourly.
Refund handling. A refund can be issued within sixty days of the original charge. Partial refunds are prorated against remaining service days.
Search indexing pipeline. Documents are chunked, embedded and written to the vector store. Reindexing is required after changing the chunking configuration.
Search result ranking. Candidate documents from lexical and vector retrieval are merged, then a cross encoder reorders the merged candidate set.
Rate limits. Each API key is limited to one thousand requests per minute. Exceeding the limit returns a 429 with a Retry-After header.
Webhook delivery guarantees. Webhooks are delivered at least once. Consumers must deduplicate on the event identifier because retries can duplicate delivery.
Audit logging. Privileged actions are written to the audit log with the acting principal, the affected resource and a timestamp. Audit entries are immutable.
OAuth scopes. A scope grants a specific capability. Scopes are additive and cannot be narrowed after a grant is issued without reauthorisation.
Session expiry. Interactive sessions end after twelve hours of inactivity. A refresh extends the session without a new sign in.
